messages:
Jin (oncall): incident-bot page: HIGH severity - gpu-pool-south-1 exhausted > 80% queueing. seen at 1932109876

incident-bot: [ALERT] gpu-pool-south-1 autoscaler reached max_replicas. queue growth detected, mean queue length +260% in 3m. Pager duty: @Jin (oncall), @Sam (sre)

Jin (oncall): I'm on it. first check: rollout v4.1 started ~1932109000. any deploy info? @deploy-bot status?

deploy-bot: deploy v4.1 -> model-green rolled to 55% of traffic in south-1 at 1932108900. Canary passed perf checks but those were with 512 token contexts.

Aisha (infra): watching GPU utilization: lots of long-lived sessions, NVMe IOPS spike, KV cache misses high. looks like context-length distribution jumped — p99 context length moved from 1200 -> 3600 over last 10m.

Mike (runtime): that explains it. v4 model's kv-cache indexing changed; warmup sequences longer and we can't amortize KV cache loads. per-instance tokens/sec down ~35%. autoscaler reacts to CPU rather than GPU mem so it's slow to spin new nodes.

Sam (sre): current symptom: request queueing at load-balancer. Throttles firing: 503s for some requests, tokens-per-second quotas exceeded for a few customers. recording customerIDs with errors now.

Charlotte (support): pulling error samples from the last 20m — several paying customers in APAC experiencing timeouts. Raising priority with CS and sending hold message to top 5 affected accounts.

Jin (oncall): mitigation plan options: 1) rollback v4.1 to v4.0 traffic split immediately; 2) manually increase gpu-pool-south-1 capacity (if available) + bump autoscaler limits; 3) enable fallback to smaller quantized model for large contexts. Thoughts?

Mike (runtime): rollback fastest to reduce per-request cost. But we need to confirm v4.0 is compatible with current routing rules. If we rollback, KV cache eviction should drop and throughput recover. I can start rolling rollback if infra gives green.

Aisha (infra): autoscaler is at hard cap (max_replicas=40 for south-1). We have spare GPUs in us-east-2 but cross-region latency may be bad for some users. Manual scale-up requires approval (quota). Requesting quota increase from cloud console now — may be 12-18m.

Sam (sre): immediate short-term: enable selective throttling for non-premium tenants to reduce pressure. We can also lengthen request timeouts to avoid cascading retries. I'll push throttle rules in 60s.

Jin (oncall): do rollback and push throttles. Charlotte coordinate with CS for affected customers, message template: "We detected increased request latencies & errors after a model rollout; we are rolling back & will follow up".

Charlotte (support): acknowledged. Drafting message now. tagging top customers for proactive heads-up.

Mike (runtime): starting rollback: running rollout_cancel --target=traffic-split:v4.0 --region=south-1

Mike (runtime): logs: 
```
INFO 1932110045 rollback initiated by mike
INFO 1932110051 routing: shifting traffic 10% -> v4.0
INFO 1932110103 routing: 55% -> 100% v4.0 completed
```

Mike (runtime): rollback shows traffic back to v4.0 at 1932110103. Observability dashboard: tokens/sec trend beginning to recover.

Aisha (infra): GPU utilization trending down. queue length p50 reduced to near baseline within 3m of rollback. KV cache miss rate dropping. autoscaler leaving extra nodes idle but not scaling down immediately due to cooldown.

Sam (sre): applying selective throttling for non-premium: 
```
route: /generate
if tenant.tier != "enterprise": rate_limit = 60rps
```
Applied at 1932110230. This cut incoming request rate by estimated 20%.

Charlotte (support): sent customer messages at 1932110300. one partner asked for ETA; we gave tentative 30m-1h while we monitor.

Jin (oncall): status update: rollback completed, queueing reduced, no full pool failures. impact: short 10-25s timeouts for some customers during peak, a handful (~4) premium customers saw degraded performance briefly. No data loss. Next steps: root cause postmortem, add better canary for context-length/distribution, tune kv-cache warmup, update canary test to include large-context traces, consider autoscaler metric to watch GPU memory pressure/KV miss rate.

Mike (runtime): agreed. I'll instrument a synthetic large-context canary that runs during deploys. Also propose a temporary config: limit max-context-per-request for new rollout by default to 2048 tokens unless opt-in.

Aisha (infra): I'll request autoscaler quota bump and file infra task: allow rapid cross-region spillover for emergency only. Also add GPU mem pressure metric to autoscaler target (PR in infra tracker).

Sam (sre): creating incident ticket INC-1932109876 with timeline, customer impact, and mitigations. Adding playbook steps for model rollbacks.

incident-bot: incident created INC-1932109876, severity: high -> monitoring for 2h.

Jin (oncall): handing off to @Sam (sre) for follow-up during night shift. Summary for handoff: rollback done at 1932110103; throttles applied 1932110230; customer comms 1932110300; monitor until queues stable and autoscaler cooldown complete. Please escalate to infra if queueings return.

Sam (sre): taking handoff. Will coordinate postmortem owners: Mike (runtime) for model behavior, Aisha (infra) for autoscaler changes, Charlotte (support) for customer comms.

Charlotte (support): noted. I'll collect error samples and CS tickets for postmortem.

Jin (oncall): thanks team. closing pager. leaving notes in incident ticket. :thumbsup:
